data.narrative:
Mariana Minerals is a Series A-stage frontier-tech company in the Climate & Energy sector, having raised $95M+ to date. The addressable comp universe comprises one public company (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables—zero companies meet narrow filtering criteria—making traditional peer-median valuation inapplicable.

Stage-progression methodology provides the primary quantitative anchor. Using total capital raised ($95M) as a value proxy and applying a standard 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A to subsequent funding rounds yields an implied valuation of $190M. This reflects typical expansion-stage repricing dynamics within frontier energy and materials development.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $162M to $218M, centered on a median of $190M. The wide band reflects reliance on a single methodological input and the absence of meaningful peer-stage calibration. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.0x multiplier for this specific subsector, the materiality of capital deployed versus operational milestones, and the absence of revenue or clinical/technical data points that would anchor later-stage valuations. Additional comparable transactions or clearer disclosure of development progress would materially improve precision.
